user.title: Add to Timerify
user.description: Add a timer to an entity, or set up the voice sentences for the built-in agent.

target.title: Add a timer
target.description: Pick the entity that the timer turns on and off.

data_description.target: The switch, light, fan or other entity to run on a timer.
data_description.mode: Strict runs the entity only while the timer counts down. Loose also lets it run without a timer.
data_description.runtime: A Runtime sensor adds up how long the target is on, by Timerify or by hand, for daily and weekly statistics.
data_description.run_for_max: The end of the Run for slider, in minutes, up to 1440 (one day). Actions, voice, pending commands and schedules can still run the device for up to a day.
data_description.off_button: Adds a Turn off button to the device page. Pressing it stops the countdown and turns the device off. It also turns off a device that runs without a countdown.

voice_settings.title: Voice settings
voice_settings.description: Timerify can write its voice sentences for the built-in agent to a file named timerify.yaml in the folder of each language you pick under custom_sentences (for example custom_sentences/en/timerify.yaml), with the names of your timers' devices in them. Timerify rewrites the files whenever a timer changes, and removes them when you untick the option, or disable or remove this entry. Do not edit them.

duration.title: Default duration
duration.description: How long the entity runs when it is turned on without a duration.

limit.title: Turn off if left on for
limit.description: A loose timer lets the entity run without a countdown. If it is left running like that, Timerify turns it off after this time. A run you ask for, such as for 3 hours, is never cut. Leave the box empty for no limit.

data.limit: Turn off if left on for

data_description.limit: In minutes, from 1 to 1440 (one day). It counts from the moment Timerify sees the entity on with no countdown.

workday.title: Workday sensor
workday.description: Schedule intervals can run on working days or on non-working days, as a Workday sensor tells them. Pick the sensor, or leave this empty if no interval of this timer needs one.

data_description.workday_sensor: A sensor of the Workday integration, set up for your country and working week. Give it a day offset of 0: the schedule asks it about the day itself.

error.target_not_supported: A timer cannot turn this entity on and off. Pick another one.
error.not_switchable: This entity does not report on or off, so a timer cannot tell whether it is running. Pick another one; if it is unavailable now, try again when it is back.
error.duration_not_whole: The duration must be a whole number of minutes.
error.duration_above_maximum: The default duration must not be longer than the maximum of Run for.

abort.already_configured: This entity already has a timer.
abort.already_in_progress: A timer for this entity is already being added.
abort.voice_settings_exist: The voice settings are already set up. Change them from the Timerify page.

user.description: The entity runs from the start time to the end time on the days you pick. An end time earlier than the start time carries the interval past midnight into the next day.

data_description.end: When the interval ends, in whole minutes. Earlier than the start means the next day.

options.strict: Strict: runs only while the timer counts down
options.loose: Loose: may also run without a timer

add_time.name: Add time
add_time.description: Adds minutes to the countdown of a timer, or takes them off with a negative number. Adding to a timer that is not running starts it; taking off all the time that is left turns the entity off. A countdown never goes beyond one day.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How many minutes to move the end of the countdown by, up to a day either way.

run.name: Run
run.description: Turns the entity on, for the minutes given. Without minutes, an entity that is off runs to the end of the schedule window that is open, if there is one; strict mode keeps the default duration when it ends later. With no window open, it runs for the default duration in strict mode and without a countdown in loose mode, where the limit of the timer, if it has one, turns it off in the end. One that is already running keeps its countdown or its limit. The settings given are applied if the entity supports them.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How long to run, in whole minutes, up to a day. Without it an entity that is off runs to the end of the schedule window that is open, if there is one; strict mode keeps the default duration when it ends later. With no window open, it runs for the default duration in strict mode and without a countdown in loose mode, where the limit of the timer, if it has one, turns it off in the end. One that is already running keeps its countdown or its limit.

stop.name: Stop
stop.description: Ends the countdown of a timer and turns the entity off, as setting Run for to 0 does. It also turns off an entity that runs without a countdown in loose mode. An entity that is off is left as it is.

add_command.name: Add command
add_command.description: Keeps a command to turn the entity on or off at a time you choose, a number of minutes from now or at a moment. A command to turn on can run for some minutes and set the entity up with the settings given. It is carried out at its time whatever state the entity is in then, and using the entity by hand does not cancel it. The response holds the command's id, which cancels it.

action.name: Action
action.description: Whether to turn the entity on or off at that time.

delay.name: Delay
delay.description: In how many minutes to carry the command out, up to a week. Give this or a time, not both.

at.name: Time
at.description: When to carry the command out, up to a week ahead. A time without a time zone is in Home Assistant's time zone. Give this or a delay, not both.

minutes.name: Minutes
minutes.description: How long a command to turn on runs, in whole minutes, up to a day. Without it the entity runs to the end of the schedule window that is open then, if there is one; strict mode keeps the default duration when it ends later. With no window open, it runs for the default duration in strict mode and without a countdown in loose mode, where the limit of the timer, if it has one, turns it off in the end. A command to turn off takes none.

cancel_command.name: Cancel command
cancel_command.description: Cancels a pending command before its time. Aim the call at the timer that holds the command; another timer does not know it. The id is in the response of Add command and in the attributes of the Next command sensor.

command_id.name: Command ID
command_id.description: The id of the command to cancel.

countdown_started.name: Countdown started
countdown_started.description: Triggers when a timer that was not counting down starts a countdown: by an action, by hand in strict mode, by a pending command or by a schedule window. It also triggers when a loose timer sets a limit on an entity that was left on with no countdown: the variable limit is then true. A change of a countdown that is already running does not trigger it.

countdown_ended.name: Countdown ended
countdown_ended.description: Triggers when the countdown of a timer ends. Its reason says how: expired when it ran out, stopped when Timerify stopped it, turned_off when the entity was switched off outside Timerify, limit when the limit of an entity left on turned it off.

command_due.name: Pending command came due
command_due.description: Triggers when a pending command of a timer comes due and is carried out. It gives the id of the command and whether it turns the entity on or off.

confirm.title: Delete the timer {timer}
confirm.description: The entity {target} that the timer {timer} switches no longer exists in Home Assistant. Until it is back, the timer switches nothing. Its countdown and pending commands are kept. If you add the device again with the same entity ID, the timer works again by itself and this message goes away. Submit to delete the timer, with its entities, schedule intervals and pending commands.

abort.issue_gone: This problem is no longer open. Nothing needs to be done.

stored_timer_invalid.title: The stored state of the timer {timer} cannot be read

confirm.title: Reset the stored timer
confirm.description: Timerify cannot read the file in which the timer {timer} keeps its countdown and pending commands: {reason}. The timer does not run until the file is reset. Resetting keeps the timer, its settings, its schedule intervals and its runtime total. It clears the countdown and the pending commands, and switches every schedule interval back on. Submit to reset it.

abort.issue_gone: This problem is no longer open. Nothing needs to be done.
abort.reload_failed: The stored timer was reset, but the timer could not be loaded again. Open the timer's page to see why.

settings_not_taken.title: The schedule interval "{interval}" of the timer "{timer}" has settings the device does not take
settings_not_taken.description: The schedule interval "{interval}" of the timer "{timer}" turns the device on with settings that the device does not take now: {settings}. Timerify keeps them, and leaves them out when the interval turns the device on. If the device takes them again, they are used again and this message goes away. If the form of the interval shows a setting, pick a value the device takes. To drop a setting the form no longer shows, delete the interval and add it again.
